mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic expansion where labor market strength and supply capacity are both growing, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where both PAYEMS and INDPRO show positive growth.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 2000 thousand units and a concurrent drop in retail sales (RSAFS) below 350000 million dollars signal weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances meeting the trigger condition during late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the core consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to aggressive monetary policy tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with CPIAUCSL growth > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly real GDP growth (GDPC1) falls below 1.0% annualized, it indicates a weakening economy, which triggers a flight to safety and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of quarters with GDPC1 growth < 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery phase, a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for two consecutive months signals strong job creation and rising consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 and a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals a supply shock combined with monetary tightening, which reduces corporate profitability and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances meeting the trigger condition.
